messages.game.546580e7b7bb5523: Roads across Japan begin at this bridge. But... no one can read the numbers on its signposts.
messages.game.3665e33fd7d2c66d: 一, 二, 三... One, two, three. We count them one by one, starting here.
messages.game.45fb19781aceb074: That's why this is number 一: one. If you can read the signposts, you can go anywhere.
messages.game.f292047168a7d2d2: Someone on the road said, 'People used to count these as they walked.'
messages.game.6c5ed7e72fec0d18: This place is called the Woods of Ueno.
messages.game.0c0eb0a10b587cbe: A child is lost in those woods. They can't read the signposts.
messages.game.c13576b5fff89a51: The sign says 森 (forest). The character has three 木 (trees).
messages.game.d1e7cde5157be756: This whole park is the 森 (forest). ...There! We've found the child!
messages.game.41f2174dfeab8082: The child's mother said, 'We've lost the habit of looking at written characters.'
messages.game.3ef6b7b5ac036964: A town where boats travel along a large 川 (river).
messages.game.e6bfd4d2774f29b3: But today the boats aren't running, because no one knows today's weather.
messages.game.e44957de4f35b4f7: 雨 (rain) looks like drops falling from the 空 (sky).
messages.game.8d97457bc64cb553: No rain today. ...There goes the boat!
messages.game.43bd8f51872e2447: The boatman said this: 'Just asking out loud will do the trick.'
messages.game.ef1e214caf9da488: Today, there's a fire festival at the temple on this 山 (mountain).
messages.game.0b0b27bb2c240c90: But no one can read the sign for 火 (fire), so nobody is coming.
messages.game.a1569de86cf56d74: 火 (fire) looks like burning flames. ...Everyone is gathering now.
messages.game.a5133dc54030f4e3: The mountaintop has turned red. ...Have you noticed? More and more KanjiMon are running wild.
messages.game.90106055f0c08c62: A person from the mountain said this: 'Voices can't reach the top of the mountain.'
messages.game.7ab88a17f4206c30: 名 (name) is a sign we call out with our 口 (mouth).
messages.game.f099ba840cfb5a7e: A name no one calls fades away. ...The same happens to written characters.
messages.game.0ebd7c386075e5ef: The child from earlier said this: 'You don't have to push yourself to memorize it.'
messages.game.fa8e4574a07262bf: The station has many trains, 電車. Every destination is written with 字 (characters).
messages.game.be023c382af229d9: But no one can read them, so nobody can board.
messages.game.726ff71a46430b2e: 町 (town), 村 (village), 学 and 校 (school)... Every destination is written in characters. Read them, and you can go anywhere.
messages.game.a1b219a38d1b1cd8: ...Look. Someone has been adding reading aids to the signs, one by one.
messages.game.351534316c9348a8: A station worker said this: 'There was someone who taught them out loud, again and again.'
messages.game.ebb26f729328fc2b: This is a new town built on top of the sea.
messages.game.3b6203ae6fabbe96: The streets all have the same shapes, so everyone gets lost.
messages.game.60428afad0a5114d: Look from 上 (above) on the Ferris wheel. ...See? Now you can make out the roads.
messages.game.7a34c9a61488b292: 上 (up), 下 (down), 左 (left), 右 (right). With these direction characters, you won't get lost.
messages.game.b7f4b5f0d1547cd6: A delivery worker said this: 'Someone's voice will read the map for you, too.'
messages.game.e14de3f1c7b3fbb9: This town began from this castle. It is the oldest place in Tokyo.
messages.game.85c843ca3c91c11c: A giant lantern with this town's name written on it.
messages.game.08b798e8f8887f55: The people of Tokyo, in particular, stopped reading the characters.
messages.game.7c1d9d050143e2ea: If no one reads them, the characters forget how to be read.
messages.game.1e26e93ce4544c3d: You don't have to push yourself to learn it.
